description: Brand/template proxy groups for ADD1000 and a 5-fold GroupKFold assignment. ADD1000 ships no brand, campaign or category labels (see folder_structure_test). Groups = Ward agglomerative clustering of L2-normalised frozen DINOv2-base CLS embeddings (448 px input) into 50 clusters, then clusters joined by an extended near-duplicate component (splits/near_dup_pairs.json) are merged (connected components). Folds: size-balanced greedy GroupKFold (largest group into the smallest fold), no group spans two folds.

folder_structure_test.verdict: The 8 release folders of 125 consecutive ids are NOT attribute categories; they are upload chunks of the id sequence. A leave-one-category-out split is therefore not written.
evidence: README names 4 bipolar dimensions (8 attributes) but ships no per-image labels; under a 4-dimension design each image carries one pole per dimension, so 8 exclusive groups of 125 cannot be attribute classes.

Folders 5-8 are split A/B (60/65 ids) and exactly these are the folders whose files exceed 25 MB in total (the GitHub web-upload file limit); folders 1-4 are 9.8-19 MB and unsplit: {"ADD1000_1": 18.8, "ADD1000_2": 14.5, "ADD1000_3": 9.5, "ADD1000_4": 15.4, "ADD1000_5A": 11.8, "ADD1000_5B": 14.4, "ADD1000_6A": 15.2, "ADD1000_6B": 17.3, "ADD1000_7A": 17.2, "ADD1000_7B": 22.2, "ADD1000_8A": 21.5, "ADD1000_8B": 23.9, "GroundTruth1000_1": 18.3, "GroundTruth1000_2": 22.3}
Pixel-identical pair 182/761 sits in folders ADD1000_2 and ADD1000_7; 391/694 (same template) in 4 and 6; 642/910 (same creative) in 6 and 8.

Linear probe on DINOv2 CLS (5-fold CV) predicting the folder of an image: accuracy at the true boundaries vs the same chunking shifted by 31/62/93 ids: {"shift_0": 0.167, "shift_31": 0.199, "shift_62": 0.176, "shift_93": 0.16, "permuted_labels_mean": 0.1268, "chance": 0.125}. Accuracy that is not peaked at shift 0 means content varies smoothly with id order, not by folder.

Kruskal-Wallis across the 8 groups on mean HSV saturation / value: p = {"saturation": 0.0125, "value": 0.0359}; same test on the 125-id chunking shifted by 31/62/93 ids: {"shift_31": {"saturation": 0.1738, "value": 0.0918}, "shift_62": {"saturation": 0.1577, "value": 0.3249}, "shift_93": {"saturation": 0.1207, "value": 0.1234}}. The colour difference is small and is a monotone drift with id (mean saturation 0.36-0.38 in folders 1-5, rising to 0.45 in folder 8; file sizes also grow with id), not the alternating pattern that paired attribute poles would produce; it is weaker for shifted chunks, so it is the one observation that does not argue against folders, but it carries no category information the content probe can pick up.

visual_check: Contact sheet of 9 images from each of the 6 largest, 2 mid-sized and 2 smallest groups (23 Nov 2026): groups are product-category / visual-style families (wine bottles; shoes; green tea and herbal products; sunglasses; pocket watches; ink-wash style real-estate and tourism posters), i.e. a plausible brand/category/template proxy; the largest group (82 ids) is a mixed bag of conceptual creative ads. Groups are a proxy, not ground-truth brands.
embedding: facebook/dinov2-base CLS token (last_hidden_state[:,0], post-layernorm), 448x448 bilinear input, ImageNet norm
